conclusion: GPU back-pressure from retained Vue terrain rendering dominates the stationary scene. The overlap shader contributes both runtime blend work and additional shader/material overhead.
frame_metric: Median Engine Cpu Time interval in milliseconds, including GPU waits. FPS is 1000/median, not presentation latency.
findings: Baseline repeats are approximately 63 ms/frame (about 16 engine FPS). Removing VSync/frame limiting does not recover throughput.
Hiding Terrain6 and Terrain7 reduces the interval from 62.723 to 26.785 ms. Disabling the procedural terrain area reduces it to 50.494 ms. These are marginal ablations, not additive costs.
Disabling overlap evaluation through width=0 saves about 10-11 ms while retaining the same main-pass primitive count.

Using the existing base material shader without overlap code reduces 62.983 to 44.594 ms. It is 8.418 ms faster than the larger overlap shader with width=0. Non-overlap material properties match exactly.

The extra static shader/material cost suggests specialization or compiler/register-pressure/resource-layout overhead; hardware occupancy or spill counters were not collected, so that mechanism is not proven.
Disabling smooth normals saves roughly 2 ms; disabling stochastic ground sampling makes little difference. Disabling graph material clipmaps provides no large recovery.

In the separate CPU trace, the main thread spends about 50 ms per frame waiting on the GPU fence. Terrain CPU render control averages about 0.8 ms per invocation; stationary height preparation is not the dominant cost.

In the controlled cache diagnostic run, update count remains 100, pending texels 0, scheduled texels 0 throughout the stationary baseline. Cache boundary updates are not causing the sustained low frame rate.
Retained Vue meshes evaluate VueTerrainOverlap directly; they do not use TerrainGraphClipmapSampling. The graph clipmap cache covers the shared procedural/composed terrain material path.
measurement_limits: Forward pass GPU timestamps are zero/unavailable in this build; use matched frame ablations, CPU fence waits and pipeline statistics instead of assigning a fabricated Forward GPU duration.

After unregistering/re-registering the terrain area, disabled cache passes retain old timestamps. The resulting multi-second GPU frame envelopes are rejected; CPU frame intervals and pipeline counts remain usable.
Preview and main pipelines share pass names. Timestamp samples are preserved by flat-list ordinal; parent/child durations must not be added together.
The SDK CPU capture contains invalid UTF-8 in some dynamic region names. The raw capture is preserved, invalid name bytes are replaced for analysis, and attribution uses stable ASCII scope names.
GPU metrics and pipeline-statistics requests introduce diagnostic overhead. Baseline repeats and restored-state checks are used; this is a stationary-view profile, not a complete camera-flight study.
No optimization was applied to production shaders or LOD settings. Visibility, materials, settings, saved level and camera were restored after diagnostic cases.
recommended_next_work: Specialize retained overlap shading for the selected precision and actual contributor count, and measure precompiled shader variants to remove generic inactive paths.
Avoid evaluating stock PBR material channels before reevaluating and overwriting them during overlap blending.
If needed, cache retained Vue blended material results as well as the existing graph terrain materials; preserve authored textures, blend widths, normal response and geometry LOD.
Validate any optimization with matched captures and frame timings; do not ship disabled blending, disabled normals or lower geometry LOD as the fix.
